players.name: Bijan Robinson
players.overallWriteup: The strongest combination of three-down workload, receiving value, touchdown access, weekly reliability and ceiling on the board. Overall RB scarcity reinforces rather than creates the No. 1 ranking.

regression.explanation: Receiving yardage may regress from 2025, but overall production was not touchdown-dependent. Sustainable elements include three straight 17-game seasons, rising role, elite dual-phase production, and strong efficiency under volume. The main restraint is projecting another 820 receiving yards under a new coordinator.

players.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
players.overallWriteup: Elite efficiency, receiving value and explosive ceiling make him a legitimate 1.01 alternative. He remains just behind Bijan because the full-season bell-cow proof is slightly weaker.

regression.explanation: Touchdown rate and efficiency can regress, but expanded workload access supports the floor. His elite status is sustainable because of receiving usage, efficiency and expanded rushing access. Exact touchdown totals and yards per carry are more volatile than the overall role.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.overallWriteup: Elite or near-elite receiver profile with strong target, production and ceiling expectations. The placement reflects direct cross-position comparison rather than market ADP.

regression.explanation: The 2025 target and reception totals can decline without removing him from the elite WR tier. His production is supported by target volume, separation, route wins and yards after the catch rather than an unsustainably high touchdown rate. A decline from 129 receptions or 1,715 yards is likely, but the underlying role remains elite.
